forum.title: STemWin on stm32h743 mcu
forum.best_answer_content:
Hello,

1- TouchGFX is something (a ST graphical library), STemwin is something else (SEGGER library).

2- I don't have idea why that was removed but you can download the older version of CubeH7 **1.12.0** as shown in this screenshot and use the latest version of IAR.

![screenshot.png](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/15ac3f49-ec2e-e159-df32-2bd9d3556320.png "screenshot.png")

The library is located under Middlewares\ST\STemWin\Lib
forum.content_text:
Dear. All

I'm asking how to use STemWin on stm32h743 mcu.

How to add STemWin on STM32CubeIDE? (Current Use Version. 1.13.0)?

How can I run a project with the development board I bought? (STM32H743I-EVAL)?

In particular, I want to run the STemWin\_SampleDemo project.

I`m use IAR EWARM ver 9.xx but in stm32cubeh7-v1-12-1 and

STM32Cube\_FW\_H7\_V1.11.0

\Repository\STM32Cube\_FW\_H7\_V1.11.0\Projects\STM32H743I-EVAL\Demonstrations\STemWin

i find STemWin.ewp project which use OGLastSavedByProductVersion 8.20.2.14834.

It mean`s STemWin.ewp should compile on EWARM 8.20 or late.

Is it possible to use example on later version EWARM ?

Best regards.
forum.author: Andrij Markovsky

scraped_replies.html:
Hello, 

Normally you can use the latest version of IAR to compile and upload that example to your Eval board. Did you face an issue?

scraped_replies.author: Andrew Neil

scraped_replies.html:
Hello @Andrij Markovsky.

ST discontinued STemWin a few years ago. This means it is no longer free for new projects, and it has not been included in STM32CubeMX for quite some time.

That said, emWin is still an active GUI library, and SEGGER remains a valued ST partner. They continue to invest in supporting selected new STM32 devices.

ST’s investment in GUI software is focused on TouchGFX, which brings better UI performance, ease of use, and technical support benefits for STM32 users. In parallel, ST is also partnering with alternative GUI software providers such as SEGGER.

Best regards,
Johan
